### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via globalFilters (literal, a string literal in packagedDashboardPart; a string literal in translateDashboard))_
- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via globalFilters (literal, a string literal in packagedDashboardPart; a string literal in translateDashboard))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via subCaption (literal, a string literal in translateDashboard))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), globalFilters (literal, a string literal in packagedDashboardPart; a string literal in translateDashboard))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **138** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b291fcdae9ac6dd4152367082905cfe81ddf5fb0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8f0b676dfc519cf9324b49319dd2f066f53595ec` — the merge of head `8f538b1a442fdc9b44112ddd480a2ab61692d24b` into base `b291fcdae9ac6dd4152367082905cfe81ddf5fb0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8f0b676dfc519cf9324b49319dd2f066f53595ec && git checkout 8f0b676dfc519cf9324b49319dd2f066f53595ec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b291fcdae9ac6dd4152367082905cfe81ddf5fb0 8f538b1a442fdc9b44112ddd480a2ab61692d24b && git checkout -B drift-repro b291fcdae9ac6dd4152367082905cfe81ddf5fb0 && git merge --no-ff 8f538b1a442fdc9b44112ddd480a2ab61692d24b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b291fcdae9ac6dd4152367082905cfe81ddf5fb0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b291fcdae9ac6dd4152367082905cfe81ddf5fb0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f538b1a442fdc9b44112ddd480a2ab61692d24b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #20680 (body, triage 5895803688, claim 5898553291, os-dev-report 5900307018, seat answer 5900364303, delta report 5900438073), PR #20728 (body, file list, net diff against `origin/main` at merge-base `5757463712`, 7 files, +582 / -9), the check-runs on the head, and the governing texts on `origin/main` (ADR-0029 D9.2a, ADR-0126 Regime O, `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`, `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`). Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head, read once (no polling), posted 2026-09-29T22:49Z: 39 runs, 18 success, 5 skipped, 16 in_progress, 0 failure. In progress at the read: Build Core, Test Core 1-6, Dogfood 1-3 and Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Lint and Repo Gates, Type Check workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger. Success at the read includes Check Changeset (both runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Part-of PR must not also close its card (both runs), Spec property liveness, Type Check source gates. A green landing still waits on the in-progress set; that is the queue's second condition, not this record's.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/spec` (`./system`, published via the package `exports` map): `translateDashboard(doc, bundle, opts)` widens its accept set — `opts` goes from `ResolveOptions` to `TranslateDocumentOptions`, so the optional `packagedBase` is now accepted and acted on. RIGHT. `TranslateDocumentOptions extends ResolveOptions` and adds only that optional key, so every existing call compiles; the dispatch table `METADATA_DOCUMENT_TRANSLATORS` was already typed with `TranslateDocumentOptions`, and `translateMetadataDocument` already passed it through. `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json` pins export names only (`translateDashboard (function)`) and `api-surface-signatures.json` does not pin this function, so no regenerated spec artifact is owed by this diff; `Type Check source gates` is success on the head.
2. Without a base the output is byte-identical to `origin/main`. RIGHT, traced: `asRecord(undefined | null)` is `undefined`; `packagedDashboardPart(undefined, …)` is `undefined` for the filter, the option and the widget; `valueOverridesPackagedBase(undefined, …)` is `false` on every one of the seven guards, so every branch falls to the pre-change lookup. Pinned by the no-base control (`undefined` and `null`) in `i18n-resolver.test.ts`.
3. With a base the comparison is per string over exactly the seven strings the bundle addresses: dashboard `label` and `description`; widget `title`, `description` and sub-caption (`options.description`); global-filter `label`; static option `label`. RIGHT. Each is matched by the bundle's own key (widget `id`; filter key via `globalFilterKey`, name else field; option `String(value)`). A widget, filter or option the base lacks resolves to `{}`, so `undefined !== value` counts it as authored — the same answer `scalarOverridesPackagedBase({}, key, value)` gives for a scalar the packaged object never declared, so the object rule's "a base that declares no such scalar" is carried over exactly. An edit back to the shipped string compares equal and the catalog still applies (the ruled no-op edge). A non-string label (an inline locale map) never counts as an override, so the map route documented in `translations.mdx` is untouched. Inputs are not mutated (the copy is built as before). `translateGlobalFilter`'s signature change is module-private, not a public change.
4. `scalarOverridesPackagedBase` delegation: the exported signature (its three-key union included) is unchanged; its body is now one call to the private `valueOverridesPackagedBase`, whose body is the same three lines. RIGHT — the ADR-0029 D9.2a "one comparison, one implementation" requirement holds, and both readers on `origin/main` (`translateObject`, and the `SchemaRegistry` fold at `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:2503`) read the same predicate unchanged. Nit, not blocking: the exported predicate's doc still says its edges are "load-bearing in two places" and `TranslateDocumentOptions.packagedBase` still says "See translateObject for the rule it feeds" — both are now one caller short; belongs to the next touch of the file.
5. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (`exports["."]`, `index.ts` line 3 exports the class): `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getPackagedDashboardBase(name): unknown` is a new public method — a public-surface widening. RIGHT. The shadow case: it is `lookupArtifactItem('dashboard', name)` and nothing wider, which is `SchemaRegistry.getArtifactItem` — composite-key (`packageId:name`) scan first with `isCodeArtifactBody`, then the bare-key fallback with the same predicate (`dashboard` is not a discriminated type, so the plain three-tier path applies). It cannot return a tenant overlay: (a) a per-org overlay — the card's case — is never hydrated into the registry at all (`hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry` returns `false` for `organizationId !== null`, ADR-0005); (b) an env-wide overlay hydrates under the BARE key only, and although `mergeArtifactProtection` then grafts the artifact's `_packageId` and `_provenance` onto it (so it looks like a code body), the composite scan runs first and returns the packaged entry; (c) the bare fallback can only win when no composite entry exists, in which case nothing was grafted, `stateTenantAuthorship` leaves `_provenance: 'org'`, and `isCodeArtifactBody` excludes it. The `undefined` edges are as documented: a non-string or empty name; no registry; a registry double with neither `getArtifactItem` nor `getItem`; any throw. The doc's "a dashboard has no extension fold" is true — ADR-0126 Regime E is object and app only, and spec declares no dashboard extension. One edge that is not a tenant overlay and outside this card: two code packages shipping the same dashboard name resolve by Map insertion order, the same order `getMetaItem`'s envelope already uses.
6. "With this PR alone no served answer changes." RIGHT, from `origin/main`: `translateMetaDocument` computes `packagedBase` only when `metaType === 'object'`; `translateMetaList` passes `packagedObjectBaseOf(...)`, whose first line returns `undefined` for every type but `object`; the only other `translateMetadataDocument` caller (`rest-server.ts:10418`) is hard-coded `'object'`; no non-test source in the repo imports `translateDashboard` directly (comments only); `getPackagedDashboardBase` has no caller on the branch outside its test. The new branch is dormant until #20730.
7. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (+5): one `{file, verb: findOne, pinned: 1}` row for the new objectql test, whose `findOne` double routes through `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`; the file is the gate's GENERATED grow-only coverage ledger and the row sits alphabetically before its object sibling. RIGHT — a coverage gain, not debt.
8. `packages/objectql/src/protocol-packaged-dashboard-base.test.ts`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec` are declared objectql dependencies; the sibling `protocol-packaged-object-base.test.ts` exists on `main`; the `find` double honours `limit`; it reads nothing outside its package. RIGHT. The eight pins (packaged body, shadow immunity, the three `undefined` answers, the host-cannot-answer double, the item read serving the overlay, translation with the base in en and zh-CN with the sibling still translated, the no-base control, reset) cover the accessor and the read it feeds.

### ② Semver level

- PR body line: `Clause-②: yes` (no arm — the rule allows at most one, none required). RIGHT: both facts in ① are widenings (a new accepted key on a published function; a new public method on an exported class). The claim's original `no` was corrected in-seat at 5900364303 and the body now carries the correction.
- `.changeset/20680-spec-dashboard-catalog-override.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`. `.changeset/20680-metadata-protocol-packaged-dashboard-base.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor`. Both RIGHT under WHICH LEVEL (`pr-automation.yml`): a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface takes at least `minor`, and a `fix(` type never lowers it. `Check Changeset` is success on this head (both runs), and the level axis is live (the dev's control leg at `d89ebb8c1c` with `patch` reds it).
- Neither package removes or renames anything, so no BREAKING banner, no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. `skip-changeset` would be wrong here and is not used.
- Changeset prose, sentence by sentence: every factual sentence in both files holds against the diff and `origin/main` — the seven strings, the key matching, "counts as authored" for missing parts, byte-identical without a base, the no-op edge, "no serving layer in this release passes a dashboard base yet", the accessor reading the code-package entry only, the three `undefined` cases, "the item and list reads already serve a published org overlay by the same identity the write stored" (pinned by the objectql item-read test), "nothing is removed or renamed". TRUE.
- PR body as squash message: `Part of #20680` first line, no closing keyword anywhere in the body, and the "Part-of PR must not also close its card" check is success; the body says the card stays open for the REST face and the console renderer, which is what the seat answer 5900364303 and the delta report say too. CONSISTENT. "The tree is `origin/main` at `5757463712`" is the merge-base. TRUE. "HEAD `d89ebb8c1c` for everything below": the head differs from it by two frontmatter words only. TRUE. "The branch is 7 commits behind `origin/main`, and none of them touches these paths": the count is 12 at this read; the diffstat of `5757463712..origin/main` over the seven paths is still empty, so the load-bearing half holds and the number is a stale reading, not a false claim. "objectui imports none of these functions": not verifiable from the inputs and not load-bearing (nothing is removed or renamed; no base is passed). The measured tables and counts are the dev's runs; nothing in the diff contradicts them.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Landing site outside the original claim (spec `i18n-resolver.ts` as the measured producer; the objectql real-registry test; the pinned JSON): ANSWERED. The seat amended the claim's file surface at 5900364303; the producer is where the catalog was applied over authored text, and the fix is at the producer as PD12 requires; the objectql test sits beside its object sibling because metadata-protocol declares no `SchemaRegistry` dependency; the pinned JSON is the gate's own `--write`. Accepted.
2. Readers of the changed functions: ANSWERED, verified in ① items 4 and 6.
3. Served-answer census (0 diffs before and after across 4 dashboards, 35 views, the app list, 4 objects; admin and member; en and zh-CN; three phases): ANSWERED on the code trace in ① item 6 — no serving path can hand the dashboard translator a base on this head, so the number is what the trace predicts. The count itself is the dev's measurement and is not re-run here.
4. "No documented rule reversed": ANSWERED, no reversal. `translations.mdx` "The authored label is the default locale's text … a zh-CN bundle still works and still wins" describes the fallback chain for a package's own label against its own bundle; a served string equal to its packaged counterpart still receives the catalog, and an inline locale map never counts as an override, so that page stays true. `translations.mdx` "published items layer over the file bundles, so an authored value wins over a shipped one" concerns translation items, untouched. ADR-0029 D9.2a's sentence "an explicit override beats a packaged default" governed the object catalog and the object fold; this PR applies the same predicate to a Regime O type and does not narrow or invert it. ADR-0126 Regime O (dashboards overlay-editable, the published overlay is what every read serves) is served by the change, not contradicted. No ADR says a catalog wins over an overlay, so no new ADR is owed; the ADR ids are left in the code (PD13). The dashboard sentence for `translations.mdx` rides on #20730, correctly, since nothing is observable before it.
5. `Part of` first line: ANSWERED in ②; consistent with the body, the card and the check.
6. The throwaway REST measurement: ANSWERED. Never on the branch — the file list has no `packages/rest` path, which is what the claim (⛔ no REST edit on this branch) and triage (per-layer child) ordered; the nine-line face is #20730, `Blocked-by: #20728`.
7. `out_of_scope_findings`: ANSWERED. #20730 (open; the REST per-layer child; body carries `Blocked-by: #20728` and names both cards) and #20731 (open; the view twin) exist; the two noted carriers — objectui `DashboardRenderer` `tWidgetTitle` re-resolving client-side, and the `translations.mdx` sentence — are named on #20730 by the seat answer. Nothing left unfiled.
8. `open_questions`: both answered in-seat at 5900364303 (Q1 A: `Clause-②: yes`, both `minor`; Q2 A: dashboards only) and applied in the patch round; the delta report 5900438073 lists no open question. Nothing to escalate.
9. Not flagged by the dev, checked anyway: no governed surface in the file list (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`); the ADR anchor over `protocol.ts` is an invariant statement (D9.8/D9.9, ADR-0119), untouched by a pure insertion; runtime strings carry no tracker number (the `[#20680]` mentions are comments and changeset prose).
